newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Traders take profits in UK stock options.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Traders take profits in UK stock options.

text.p: Profit-taking may have been behind the main UK stock options deals as share prices weakened on Wednesday, dealers said.

One such deal was in British Steel when 2,000 July 160 calls were bought back at 2-1/2p. Similarly, in supermarket chain J.Sainsbury 1,000 July 360 calls were bought back at prices between 13p to 15p.
Meanwhile, the main deal in building materials group Tarmac was the sale of 2,000 June 100 calls at prices ranging between 27p and 29p.
At 1455 GMT, British Steel shares were up 2-1/2p to 151-1/4p, Sainsbury was up 1-1/2p at 363p while Tarmac shed 3p to 127p.
A volatility trade was the main deal in insurer Prudential Corporation, achieved by buying 322 August 650 puts at 24p and 322 August 700 calls at 22p in a long strangle strategy.
For a profit, the strategy requires the underlying shares to move far away from the strike prices so that at expiry Prudential shares need to be either below 604p or above 746p.
Elsewhere, one of the larger deals in FTSE 100 index options was a put spread hedged by an opposite position in FTSE futures, which established a volatility trade.

It involved buying 1,300 September 4125 puts at 15p and selling 1,300 September 4325 puts at 30p against selling futures at 4747. If the deal stays properly hedged, it will make money if market volatility decreases.
At 1455 GMT, cash FTSE had fallen 18.6 points to 4721.0 and June futures had dropped 22 to 4724.
